translationRepairs: Song Taizuo 1: he became magistrate of Anji and won repute for strict, capable rule.
Song Taiyu 1: he became magistrate of Anji and won repute for strict, capable rule.
s0005 has 宋泰豫元年; 泰豫 is the Liu Song reign name Taiyu, so Taizuo is a clear mistranslation and Song Taiyu 1 restores the correct era.
In the first year of Taizuo of Song, he was made magistrate of Anji and gained a name for stern competence.
In the first year of Taiyu of Song, he was made magistrate of Anji and gained a name for stern competence.
The literal of s0005 likewise renders 泰豫 as Taizuo; Taiyu matches the Chinese reign name without other changes.
the second year of Jianyuan: he bore the staff, supervised Ying and Yiyang in Sizhou, became champion general and inspector of Ying, and was raised to general who conquers the barbarians.
In the second year of Jianyuan: he bore the staff, supervised Ying and Yiyang in Sizhou, became champion general and inspector of Ying, and was raised to general who conquers the barbarians.
The idiomatic of s0011 begins with lowercase “the,” which is not a grammatical sentence start; adding “In” and capitalizing fixes a real error while leaving the rest of the wording intact.
In the fifth year he took the staff, supervised Xiyang in Ying and Runan in Si, became right general and inspector of Yu.
In the fifth year he took the staff, supervised Yuzhou together with Xiyang in Yingzhou and Runan in Sizhou, became right general and inspector of Yu.
s0019’s 監豫州郢州之西陽司州之汝南二郡軍事 includes 豫州 in the supervision scope; the idiomatic had omitted Yuzhou from that clause while keeping only inspector of Yu, and the proposed wording restores it.
Day wuzi: Bao Juan was made crown prince; every man who had become a father gained one rank; filial sons, worthy grandsons, righteous men, and faithful widows were sought out, praised, and rewarded.

Day wuzi: Bao Juan was made crown prince; every man who stood as heir to his father gained one rank; filial sons, worthy grandsons, righteous men, and faithful widows were sought out, praised, and rewarded.
賜天下爲父後者爵一級 uses 爲父後者 for agnatic heirs who stand as successors to their fathers, not men who had become fathers; the proposed idiomatic corrects that semantic error.

Day wuzi: the crown prince Bao Juan was established; all who had become fathers received one rank; filial sons, obedient grandsons, men of righteousness, and chaste wives were broadly singled out, commended, and promoted.

Day wuzi: the crown prince Bao Juan was established; all who were heirs to their fathers received one rank; filial sons, obedient grandsons, men of righteousness, and chaste wives were broadly singled out, commended, and promoted.
The same 爲父後者 in the literal of s0064 was mistranslated as those who had become fathers; “heirs to their fathers” restores the technical sense.

Eleventh month, day guiyou: Staff Clerk of the West Central Corps Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an was made Inspector of Yangzhou; Administrator of Jinshou Wang Hongfan was made Inspector of Qing and Ji; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan additionally led the Crown Prince's Junior Tutor.

Eleventh month, day guiyou: Staff Clerk of the West Central Corps Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an was made Inspector of Yangzhou; Administrator of Jinshou Wang Hongfan was made Inspector of Qing and Ji; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan additionally held the Crown Prince's Junior Tutor.
尚書令王晏領太子少傅 uses 領 for concurrent tenure of the junior-tutor office; “led” misreads that formula, and “held” is accurate.
Mian, marquis of Anlu, was posthumously raised to prince of Anlu.
Mian, Marquis Zhao of Anlu, was posthumously raised to prince of Anlu.
追贈安陸昭侯緬爲安陸王 includes the posthumous epithet 昭; omitting it from the idiomatic drops part of the Chinese title, and Marquis Zhao of Anlu restores it.
A second edict said: "Food is the people's heaven—the Book of Ji sets its meaning high; silkworms are the root of living—the canon of Xuan gives their teaching weight.
A second edict said: "Food is the people's heaven—the Ji records set its meaning high; silkworms are the root of living—the canon of Xuan gives their teaching weight.
義高姬載 alludes to Ji (Zhou) records/writings parallel to 軒經, not a discrete titled “Book of Ji”; “the Ji records” removes the invented book title.
Seventh month of autumn, day xinwei: Prince Bao Yi of Jin'an, right general, took South Xu.
Seventh month of autumn, day xinwei: Prince Bao Yi of Jin'an, right general, was made inspector of South Xu.
以…爲南徐州刺史 is an appointment as inspector; “took South Xu” drops 刺史 and can read as conquest, while “was made inspector of South Xu” matches the Chinese.
Eighth month, day dingwei: Prince Bao Yuan of Luling, right guards general, took South Yan.
Eighth month, day dingwei: Prince Bao Yuan of Luling, right guards general, was made inspector of South Yan.
爲南兖州刺史 likewise marks an inspector appointment; replacing “took South Yan” with “was made inspector of South Yan” restores the office.
Third year, spring, first month, day dingmao: Yang Chongzu, son of Yang Gui of Yinping, was made inspector of Sha and enfeoffed as prince of Yinping.
Third year, spring, first month, day dingmao: Yang Chongzu, son of Yang Gui, Prince of Yinping, was made inspector of Sha and enfeoffed as prince of Yinping.
陰平王楊炅 titles the father Prince of Yinping; “Yang Gui of Yinping” understates 王, and “Yang Gui, Prince of Yinping” restores the rank.

Fifth month, day jisi: Xiao Yi, suppressing-the-barbarians general, took Yi; Yin Guangzong, vanguard general, took Liang and South Qin; Li Qingzong, newly relieved of Ning, was again made inspector of Ning.

Fifth month, day jisi: Xiao Yi, suppressing-the-barbarians general, took Yi; Yin Guangzong, vanguard general, took Liang and South Qin; Li Qingzong, previously newly appointed inspector of Ning, was again made inspector of Ning.
前新除寧州刺史 uses 新除 for a prior fresh appointment, not relief from office; “previously newly appointed inspector of Ning” corrects the false “relieved.”

Fifth month, day jisi: Suppressing-the-Barbarians General Xiao Yi was made Inspector of Yi; Vanguard General Yin Guangzong was made Inspector of Liang and South Qin; Li Qingzong, newly relieved as inspector of Ning, was again made Inspector of Ning.

Fifth month, day jisi: Suppressing-the-Barbarians General Xiao Yi was made Inspector of Yi; Vanguard General Yin Guangzong was made Inspector of Liang and South Qin; Li Qingzong, previously newly appointed as Inspector of Ning, was again made Inspector of Ning.
The literal of s0131 makes the same error on 前新除; “previously newly appointed as Inspector of Ning” matches the bureaucratic formula.
Second month, day guichou: Xiao Hui, left guards general on leave, bore the staff and marched to relieve Shouyang.
Second month, day guichou: Xiao Huixiu, left guards general, bore the staff of authority and marched to relieve Shouyang.
遣左衛將軍蕭惠休假節援壽陽 parses as Xiao Huixiu plus 假節 (staff of authority), not Xiao Hui on leave; the proposed idiomatic fixes both the name and the office formula.
Second month, day guichou: Left Guards General Xiao Hui on leave of absence bore the staff and went to aid Shouyang.
Second month, day guichou: Left Guards General Xiao Huixiu, bearing the staff of authority, went to aid Shouyang.
The literal likewise splits 蕭惠休 and misreads 假節 as leave; Xiao Huixiu bearing the staff of authority restores the Chinese.
Xiao Yingke, rear army chief clerk, took South Yan.
Xiao Yingzhou, rear army chief clerk, took South Yan.
蕭穎胄 is Xiao Yingzhou; Yingke misreads 胄, and the proposed name correction is accurate.
Rear Army Chief Clerk Xiao Yingke was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.
Rear Army Chief Clerk Xiao Yingzhou was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.
The literal of s0176 has the same Yingke error for 蕭穎胄; Xiao Yingzhou is the correct romanization.
Tasks of the heart and sinew may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Hui on leave, and Cui Huijing."
Tasks of the heart and sinew may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Huixiu, and Cui Huijing."
心膂之任可委…蕭惠休… lists the personal name Huixiu with no leave formula; “Xiao Hui on leave” is a false parsing, and Xiao Huixiu is correct.
Tasks of the heart and sinew may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Hui on leave, and Cui Huijing."
Tasks of the heart and sinew may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Huixiu, and Cui Huijing."
The literal of s0185 repeats the same misreading of 蕭惠休; replacing “Xiao Hui on leave” with Xiao Huixiu restores the name.
Shamans and spirit-mediums said: "The headwaters of Rear Lake pass through the palace grounds, causing the emperor's illness.」
Shamans and spirit-mediums said: "The headwaters of Rear Lake pass through the palace grounds, causing the emperor's illness."
The English literal closes the quotation with a Chinese corner bracket 」 instead of "; swapping to an English closing quote is a real orthographic fix with no semantic change.
Attendants reported: "If the Grand Provisioner lacked this water it could not operate.」
Attendants reported: "If the Grand Provisioner lacked this water it could not operate."
s0203’s literal likewise ends with 」 in the English field; an English closing quotation mark is the correct repair.
He cast off kinsmen of the shared patrimony before they cast him off;
He cast off first the kinsmen who shared the same inheritance, while power was still his;

令同財之親，在我而先棄 means he cast off shared-patrimony kin first while power was still his; “before they cast him off” invents a reciprocal act absent from the Chinese, and the proposal removes that invention.
Dread and doubt ran deep; every glance seemed an outsider's plot. He wept and killed—and no man called it justice. If a throne is held by fear alone, what night is free of shame?

Suspicion and timidity ran deep; mistrust seemed to come from without. He wept as he carried out executions—not called a righteous act; if one seeks only safety in the affair, how can there be no inner shame?
事苟求安，能無內愧？ asks whether seeking only safety can be free of inner shame; the idiomatic’s throne-by-fear and sleepless-night imagery is invented, and the proposed wording tracks the Chinese.
